newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen off $0.50-$1.00-trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen off $0.50-$1.00-trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Monday were seen $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower, pressured by projections for weaker pork prices, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
Top prices in Iowa and southern Minnesota for hogs delivered to plants could range from $57.50 to $59.00, with $59.00 seen as an extreme top.
Illinois top prices at the plant were seen at $57.00 to $57.50.
Indiana/Ohio top prices on animals delivered to the plant could range from $56.50 to $57.50, sources there said.

Larger-than-expected interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog marketings Thursday and field reports of hogs putting on extra pounds as farmers concentrated on harvesting, lent pressure to the pork market as supplies mounted, market sources said.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota marketings Thursday totaled 111,000 head, well over the day's estimate of 105,000, USDA said.
Fresh retail pork cuts at midday were trading slowly, with hams down $2.00 to $5.00 per cwt and seedless bellies and trimmings untested, according to USDA.
